Generally, in the case of personal data deletion there are only a few limited exceptions where companies could still keep the data. Therefore, I would suggest that when you submit the ticket to privacy you further detail the business need(s) to potentially access the data.

[~accountid:5d428497e4777b0db2f0e20a] This is something that will positively affect any PR:

* PR reviews will immediately become easier. Right now, if you want to test UI/UX, you have to either:
* Switch to that branch locally – most of the time this requires a restart of the admin-panel which takes several minutes (plus minor but measurable inconvenience of having to stash your current work)
* Or start a new pipeline yourself, deploy to prelive and test it there. Again, this takes several minutes.
* Ask the author to provide some GIFs or screen recordings.
* Forget about it and ignore UI/UX. Click {{approve}} because the code is mostly OK.

In practice, we use all 4 of these, and it’s not amazing. Would have been so much easier to just click on a URL and see the changes.

* Showcasing your work to affected parties (e.g. users) will become possible/easy. Right now, if you want to do it, you have to either:
* Start a pipeline and deploy your branch to LIVE/PRELIVE without merging. Of course this blocks your teammates, so just tell them they should feel free to rollback/cancel your pipeline if needed. Another alternative, I think, is to cancel the pipeline without rolling back the changes, but that can be problematic.
* Just record some GIFs. Obviously, this usually raises lots of questions about additional/related functionality and how this change affects it – it’s really easier to let the user interact with the page instead of just showing GIFs.

Again, in practice, we use all of the options. We’ve done long-running pipelines (for a few weeks) for a major change, and for everything else with use GIFs, but the situation is less than ideal and again it would have been so much easier to just share a URL.

* This is a positive general change for developer velocity. As a rule of thumb, we usually open prelive and then live to double-check our changes. Sometimes we notice minor issues and want to change something. Doing this through the builder turns the situation into a very long “edit-compile-run” cycle, which is why I created [https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/PIF-811|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/PIF-811|smart-link]. If the branch build is started immediately after the changes are pushed, it could very well be that the build is ready and deployed while the developer was doing something else (e.g. writing a description for the PR), so the changes can be tested immediately.

* For the reasons stated above (people starting pipelines just to test things or show the work to others), there can be less blocking of your teammates. Our team works on 1 package (in general, we work on 1 page only). This means that any pipeline to deploy changes will be locked by any pipeline to test a PR or show someone their changes. Right now there are these possible workarounds:
* You can merge changes without deploying. Just fire and forget. For most people, this is scary AF. There’s still a lock but in practice, it’s much shorter. However, the next person to deploy their changes will bring your changes to PRELIVE/LIVE, and they might not be aware of it.
* Just work at a different time… At night is best. Avoid times when people are more likely to push their changes (e.g. before standups, before sprint plannings, etc.)

Again, we use a mix of these. I’m an advocate for “merge without deploying” approach. Others are mostly against it, but they almost never notice that they’re deploying my changes along with their changes, so it sort of works. 🙈 
This might seem like an unrelated problem, but the thing is that by minimizing the number of pipelines people need to start we can free the time for the pipelines that are actually useful (those when you actually want to deploy to LIVE).


I probably missed some other wins, but what do you think [~accountid:5d428497e4777b0db2f0e20a], is this enough and are the improvements to the dev experience clear?

One counter-example is the existence of the neglected [https://github.com/bolteu/admin-framework-components|https://github.com/bolteu/admin-framework-components|smart-link] repository. We do stumble upon minor issues in its components, but the bar for making any changes there is too high (you’d need a PR to that repo + approval + the release process + bump of the version in the admin panel, and before that, of course, linking the custom version locally for testing which is sometimes problematic). Many people rely on these components often, but there are just a few fixes yearly. It’s easier to work around issues or wrap around the components than dealing with that repo. It’s a perfect example of why code related to the same project should ideally be in the same repo – the dev experience is much better, and the process just flows.

So the half-serious answers to the questions are:

* No.
* No. Large monorepos work. In our case, it’s not a monorepo, and it’s not that large. Don’t worry.
* Don’t do it; it’s free 🙂 

On a more serious note, there is some work required to make it work in the long run. For example, I remember some discussion about build times being long, and one of the steps is doing a {{git clone --depth 1,}} which alone takes several seconds. This is just one of the things that needs to be done right, and it can take some PINT dev time. In this particular case – {{git pull}} is significantly faster than a clone. For example, with my local setup, getting 1 month (!!!) worth of bolt-server changes with git pull is 30% faster than cloning the repo with {{--depth 1}}. So, if you can keep any repo state in the build image (and fetch/unpack that build image efficiently or proactively), you can keep things fast even if the repo continues to become larger. But that’s just one specific issue.

No, unless this is highly configurable per team/repo/module/etc. Most of the tickets for our team are for admin-panel only and there’s really no need to prevent people from doing minor/medium work there at any time they find comfortable. Otherwise you’ll just slow down the development for no good reason at all, we (our team) have never had any incident related to people working after office hours.

Foreign keys in MySQL can cause performance issues on large datasets for several reasons:

# *Checking Constraints*: Whenever you add or update data, MySQL must check foreign key constraints. This can slow down data insertion and updates.
# *Indexing*: Foreign keys usually require indexing. While indexes speed up queries, they slow down data modification operations like insert, update, and delete, because the indexes need to be updated.
# *Locking*: In InnoDB, foreign keys can cause row-level locks beyond the actual rows being inserted, updated, or deleted. This can impact performance, especially on large datasets.
# *Complex Joins*: Queries involving foreign keys often require joins. Complex joins on large datasets can be slow.
# *Cascade Operations*: If you use cascade delete or update, MySQL must update or delete related rows, which can be a heavy operation on large datasets.

*TO DRIVER*

*Assunto: Notificação para prestação de informações*

Caro Sr. Carlos,

Recebemos notificação para prestação de informações relativamente à Reclamação EDOC 1972/2023.

Conforme já oportunamente tivemos a oportunidade de informar o Sr. Carlos,  foi identificado como tendo um comportamento fraudulento na plataforma Bolt. De acordo com o artigo 8º da Lei n.o 45/2018 de 10 de agosto (Regime jurídico da atividade de transporte individual e remunerado de passageiros em veículos descaracterizados a partir de plataforma eletrónica),  “Só podem ser recusados os serviços de TVDE que: a) Impliquem a circulação em vias manifestamente intransitáveis pelo difícil acesso ou em locais que ofereçam notório perigo para a segurança do veículo, dos passageiros ou do motorista; b) Sejam solicitados por pessoas com comportamento suspeito de perigosidade; c) Sejam solicitados de forma incompatível com o previsto na presente lei.” Acresce que, de acordo com o artigo 14(2) da mesma lei, a Bolt “deve bloquear o acesso aos serviços prestados pela mesma por parte dos operadores de TVDE, motoristas ou veículos que incumpram qualquer dos requisitos referidos na presente lei, sempre que disso tenha ou devesse ter conhecimento.”

The reference that has been made in the comment below is “section 115 (7 & 8) Part V Police Act 1997” in my view this reference does not give Bolt a legal basis to share this data with the prospective employer who has requested this information. 

The Police Act 1997 section 7 & 8 is referencing the powers that the police exercise when disclosing information relevant to an Enhanced Disclosure Barring Check, there is no reference in this legislation indicating that Bolt needs to provide any information. 

Based on the information provided so far and if the only legislation referenced is the Police Act 1997 I cannot see any legal basis for Bolt to share this information, therefore would resist in sharing the data. 

Generally speaking, once an employer receives the DBS check it is usually up to them to decide how they will proceed based on the information they are provided with. In this instance the prospective employer has stated to you that they are aware of the following _"From the information made available to me, on 04-07-2023, Bolt reported to the police that an allegation of inappropriate touching was made against Frank by a female passenger._ The matter was filed by the Police, therefore usually the employer would make a decision depending on the job role (if the job involves vulnerable adults and/or children) based on the outcome in the DBS, I am not sure why they have approached Bolt for internal investigation paperwork, it would make more sense for them to gain information from the relevant police force that this matter was reported to.

+*The ideal solution*+ - to be on the safe side -  would be to *deactivate the feature component triggering the loss of the place in the virtual queue*, should the driver refuse the order and de-risk the feature in light of the Labour Deal restrictions. 



+*Mitigation*+ 

*However,* I understand that by doing so, drivers will wait in line until they receive the desired ride order and they will be more incline to refuse small journey/low value orders and this might be *detrimental to passengers' experience*.

* triggering the loss of place in the virtual queue only after several refuses in a row so that in practice “prioritisation of job offers” will occur fewer times 
* while waiting in the virtual queue drivers should be able to receive orders outside the FIFO queueing system.

We have analyzed the provided documents, and *we are of the opinion that the deposit should be returned to Bolt in full*.

 

+*Handover of the property*+

* Pursuant to point 11.5 of the lease agreement, in the event of a delay in the return of the Property, the Landlord is entitled to demand payment of the Rent in double the amount for each commenced month of non-contractual use, as well as the corresponding cost of Media and any other fees due under the lease agreement until the Property is actually returned.

* In our opinion, proposal of the Landlord sent on 29 April 2022 that both parties should meet on 4 May 2022 and further phone call between the parties during which it was agreed that the Property will be handed over on 5 May 2022,  *should be considered as mutual modification of the lease agreement*. The statement in the e-mail from the Landlord dated 11 January 2024 is wrong as we assume that Bolt hired a courier company to transfer its goods on 5 May 2022 because such date was firstly agreed as the handover date by the parties.
* Additionally, please note that 3rd May is a national holiday in Poland. In such case, according to the Polish Civil Code, if an act has to be performed on a day which is e.g. a national holiday, *the deadline for such act falls on the next business day (therefore here it was 4 May 2022).*
* As a result of the above, *point 11.5 of the lease agreement could not have been applied by the Landlord as there was no late handover of the Property by Bolt*.

+*Payment of the fee for cleaning and painting*+

* Pursuant to point 11.2 and 11.4 of the lease agreement, the offices and staff rooms should be repainted by the Tenant or the Landlord could deduct the cost of the painting service from the deposit. In addition, the company should return the premises in a tidy condition, and in the event of this violation, the Landlord was entitled to arrange cleaning of the Property at the company's expense, with a maximum cleaning cost of EUR 2 per square meter.

* The Landlord states that the cleaning and painting was made by itself, yet there is no proof that such works have been performed. In our opinion, if the handover protocol was signed by Bolt (provided copy is unsigned by Bolt), then Bolt agreed that the Property requires repainting. However, please note that pursuant to point 8.3 of the lease agreement, *before satisfying any claims against Bolt from the deposit, the Landlord is obliged to give Bolt an additional period of 7 calendar days to fulfill the obligation with a warning that if the claim is not satisfied within this additional period, it will be satisfied from the deposit amount. Only if the claim is not satisfied within this additional period, the Landlord is entitled to satisfy its claim from the deposit amount.*
* As we understand, Bolt has not been called by the Landlord to clean and repaint the Property, therefore *the Landlord has not been entitled to settle its claim from the deposit.*
* As to the fact no. 1 of your e-mail, please note that pursuant to point 8.1 of the lease agreement, the deposit covers all financial claims of the Landlord towards Bolt. In our opinion, such costs could have been settled from the deposit but only after the above procedure have taken place.

+*Recommendations*+

* Based on the above, *we are of the opinion that the deposit should be returned to Bolt in full*. It is to Bolt’s decision, whether a part of the deposit should be left to the Landlord as a result of cleaning or painting (in case it actually happened, and Landlord can provide any proof of performing such actions). Please note that if the Landlord actually cleaned or painted the property, it is entitled to demand payment from Bolt.
* At first, we recommend sending a formal letter to the Landlord, in which Bolt describes the facts and requests the deposit to be returned by the Landlord, taking into consideration the above arguments.

* If the Landlord does not return the deposit in the indicated time (e.g. 14 days), we see a possibility to initiate court proceedings in a simplified procedure and to obtain a court order obliging the Landlord to return the deposit. Please note that the Landlord has a right to appeal from such order.

# Food calls [mobility/appState/get|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/4ccca13b5abd5722e699188c2bc9d68874f6dfe3/src/platform/user/user_gateway/main/Bootstrap.ts#L308] only
# Around 95% of [mobility/appState/get/v1|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/4ccca13b5abd5722e699188c2bc9d68874f6dfe3/src/platform/user/user_gateway/main/Bootstrap.ts#L309] calls are for “complete” login state

If I understand correctly, you have a valid residence permit for residing in Estonia. Since you are also employed in Estonia on the basis of an employment contract and Bolt as your employer pays social tax, you qualify for Estonian Health Insurance. 

We have a separate Confluence page that has a lot of info about health care https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/BILP/pages/4480599611/Health+care+in+Estonia 
There's also a very useful digital file "practical information for foreigners" on this page https://www.tervisekassa.ee/en/people/health-care-services (in the blue "read more" box). 

Confido is an additional health insurance provider that has some bigger coverages. For example the dentist coverage with the basic health insurance is I think only 40€ a year which given the prices of dentist work, is nothing. 😄 Confido has a bigger coverage but please be aware that since the current policy is ending in May, the later you join, the smaller the coverage amounts. From my personal experience dentistry and mental health are the only issues that I have had bigger needs for than what the basic Estonian Health Insurance offers. Most specialist doctor visits are free with a referral from your GP or just free without a referral but there might be waiting time. So Confido is good if you don't want to wait and pay or for dentist work etc, but keep in mind that it doesn't cover all possible medical issues. And there's still the own share which is 20%. You can read about Confido here: https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/BILP/pages/3165650957/Confido+Health+Insurance 

Let me know if you still want me to add you to Confido. The current sign up date for the insurance beginning on 15/02 is 09/02. So please let me know by then and of course ask if you have any other questions. I'm here for you! 😊

Best wishes

This is a very simple request but might be confusing. 
Debt and claims query:

{noformat}select 
entity_id,
sum(amount) 
from etl_billing_balance_provider
where entity_id 
in (${list_of_ids})
and date(created_date) <= date '${end_date}'
group by 1{noformat}

Basically the balance up to the last day of the year. If positive, then it’s a claim, if negative, then it’s a debt.

Fees/commission query:

{noformat}select 
entity_id,
sum(amount) 
from etl_billing_balance_provider
where entity_id 
in (${list_of_ids})
-- start_date = first day of year, end_date = last day of year 
and date(created_date) between date '${start_date}' and  date '${end_date}'
and transaction_type = 'fee'
group by 1{noformat}

All the fees charged in the whole year, transaction_type = ‘fee’ could change next year if there is something else to be considered as Fee (first finish reading to understand more)

Sales query: 

{noformat}select 
entity_id,
sum(abs(amount)) 
from etl_billing_balance_provider
where entity_id 
in (${list_of_ids})
-- start_date = first day of year, end_date = last day of year
and date(created_date) between date '${start_date}' and  date '${end_date}'
and transaction_type = 'food'
group by 1{noformat}

All sales done by the provider related to the finished orders in the app.

Potential Commission is calculated by doing commission total / sales total, and it should be 16.06% or the current commission assigned in the Provider Profiles in Admin. Please note that if the commission changes in the middle of the year for anyone, the commission won’t be exactly the old or the new one, but a weighted average of both.

Usually they will compare with commission with sales without VAT, which is wrong, as Commission doesn’t get VAT deducted. So comparison needs to be sales with VAT and Commission with VAT, or take out VAT manually on commission, and compare with sales without VAT (although this is not done at a data level, so it’s just a manual match to explain any differences)

*CS OPS' input on the reasons for high AHT for invoice-related processes in Business* ⬇️ 

The general consensus appears to be that invoicing in general is a complex topic as:

* taxation is often complicated and Bolt does not provide clear explanations for tax topics
* invoicing is market-dependent, meaning each market will have its own complexities that agents need to learn separately
* generally this issue involves few false-positives - while on other ATIs we may get tickets which are easily solved as the issue may be on the client's side. for example, generally in invoicing clients will often request invoice regeneration/detail changes, ask for explanations for unclear details, and all of these require often undocumented actions or investigations

To be more specific, the sources of the high AHT are:

* escalations to Commerce (roughly 30% of tickets are escalated to 2nd dependencies according to my data)
* investigations in admin (finding appropriate invoices etc. - this is also made more difficult due to the issue of not having a multi-modal order search page)
* clients requesting alterations to the invoice which are not possible or have not been attempted before (language changes, adding/removing details, discount changes etc.)
* users who did not use WP for a trip and may be upset over not receiving an invoice, or WP users who did not use business payment method etc.

Possesses any written document, which can be assumed to be of importance as evidence, he is obliged to produce it; however, such obligation does not fall on the suspect in criminal cases or the person who is in such a relationship with him, as referred to in ch. 36. Section 3.

The obligation to present a written document does not apply to a memorial note or other such record, which is intended exclusively for personal use, unless there is a special reason for it to be presented.

According to practice, written documents also mean electronically stored information. Supreme Court decisions: NJA 1981 p 791, NJA 1992 p 307, NJA 2015 p 631 and 2020 p 373.

hey [~accountid:62722e092db308007024a425] and [~accountid:5f52461dfdc3f5003f51865e],

# [§ 24 BDSG|https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/englisch_bdsg/englisch_bdsg.html#p0207] applies only to private companies which need to process the data to defence the legal claim btw the company and the user, not btw the third party and the user. This para is in line with the GDPR wording and applies in the same manner - only to legal claims btw the controller (company) and the data subject (user)
# § 24 BDSG is not a legal obligation. It’s a general non-prohibition to process the data for another purpose. As per the GDPR, controller cannot use the data for another purpose if certain criteria are not satisfied. § 24 BDSG is just one of the criteria, but it still requires us to have a legal basis to process the data under Art 6 of the GDPR
# We cannot rely on the legal obligation (Art 6(c) of the GDPR) as there is no explicit law that states the companies should share data in their possession with third parties like legal firms for their clients defence. So, without this wording, we cannot rely on this basis and just share the data. We should have another legal basis
# We cannot rely on Bolt’s legitimate interest (Art 6(f) of the GDPR) as there is no Bolt’s interest. The defence is for the client, not for Bolt. So without Bolt’s interest, we cannot rely on this basis
# The last one left is only the consent (Art 6(a) of the GDPR). It means that sharing this data with the lawyers for their client’s defence can be done only when the user’s consents for Bolt to share this data and be contacted about the incident. If the user does not agree, we have to ask the lawyer to refer to the police and we will disclose this data to the police as we are obliged t share data with the police in most of the cases.

[~accountid:5f52461dfdc3f5003f51865e] please do not share user’s data with the lawyers without user’s consent. The procedure should be the following:
## Lawyer contacts us to provide data about the user
## We check and clarify the purpose and what the lawyer will do with this data
## We identify the latest user of rental services
## We contact this user to receive a consent to share their data with the lawyers for the purpose specified by the lawyer via Beehive (template for consent will be provided by us)
### If the user agrees, We can only provide first name and phone number of a person or email (not both) to the lawyer. We should also mark that this data can be used only for the purpose specified above (template for response is also on our side to prepare)
### If user disagrees, we ask the lawyer to contact the police for this case as the user does not give a consent and Bolt does not have another legal basis to share the data (template for response is also on our side)

Hey team! Wanted to update you on the outcome of this case.

I discussed the case with Commerce Fraud - turns out they can whitelist the user in such cases so the account deletion could be done even if there is a debt.

We agreed on the following process:

# User reaches out with a request to delete their account
# CS makes the checks and finds out that the account can't be deleted because of the debt in another currency
# CS escalates the case to the Fraud team via SD
# Fraud team makes the checks, whitelists the user, replies to CS
# CS proceeds with the account deletion
# Account is deleted, everybody is happy :partying_face: 

I will get this process published in the [Rider or eater requests to delete account|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360003841794] article.

According to Bolt's Option Agreement option units can be exercised 10 years after grant date and before that if the company so decides, as also highlighted in Confluence page. 

FMV means fair market value, which reflects company’s share price on the public market. Since Bolt is not publicly listed company then this means that there’s no FMV that would be applicable to be shown on Carta. 

Taking into account exercising terms in Option Agreement the exercising is not possible in Carta. 

Once 10 years has passed from the grant date then the option holder has 5 years to exercise their option units. To do that they need to fill out an Exercise Notice document, that is attached to each grant in Carta, and forward this to the Company by using an email that is listed in the Option Agreement as the Company’s contact email. 

In case of any earlier liquidity events, Bolt will reach out to all eligible option holders and notify them about such opportunity and set criteria.

Hi [~accountid:712020:ab95f96b-73f1-4bb8-a5fd-5178ef3f1339] the driver shopping feature has been introduced in 2023 to switch the power to the riders. The features allows riders to select the driver they want (instead of the platform selecting the driver) from a list of 10 drivers based on proximity.

From our last bi-weekly call, I understand there are concerns that this feature might be impacting negatively supply. Therefore, you are considering whether or not keep this feature live in Portugal. Please see below my thoughts.

*BACKGROUND*

* _Relevance of the feature in the operational minimisation strategy:_ IMO the most valuable element of this feature is that it adds one more stakeholder to the relation between Bolt and Driver, ie, the passenger. The more stakeholders are involved (fleets, passengers,..) in the platform work, the more diluted are the powers of control and direction that are central to an employer/employee relation. This is beneficial for Bolt. 
* _Not a clear understanding of the reclassification criteria:_ There are no court decisions to my knowledge in Portugal that allow us to have clarity on how will judges interpret the reclassification criteria in relation to platform workers. 
* _Reclassification risk level:_ There has not been a focus of Labour Inspector on the ride-hailing sector. However, this might change and it is something that we cannot control. 

*RECOMMENDATION*

Based on the above I continue to see a legal benefit in this feature.

*NEXT STEPS*

It would appear therefore relevant that there is a review of the value of the feature in the market in order to support you in attempting to assess risk in the commercial decision to deactivate it. Therefore, could you please confirm the following:

a) what is the loss in revenue due to this feature? how did you reached this conclusion and could we quantify it per month and in terms of %GMV?

b) this feature seems not to be mandatory. What is the percentage of riders using the feature?

While you are filling in the templates and collect wet it signatures on the final versions, I will finalise a short guidance/ procedure to be then uploaded onto Confluence but please find below already some notes.



+*Timeframes*+ 

As a reminder, regarding the financial statements for the fiscal year closed on December 31, year N they must be approved within 6 months following the end of the fiscal year, i.e., before the end of June N+1, [ _then filed with the Trade and Company Registry within a month following the decisions approving the financial statements -_ *please read below re filing]*. 

*Sanctions*: delay is approving accounts implies that legal representatives failed in his duty to inform the shareholder and present the accounts. Failing to approve of the accounts can be punished by a fine of up to EUR 9,000 and the shareholder can hold the Managers liable for damages if the failure to provide information has caused any damage. Such sentencing is very rare, especially where the accounts are filed as soon as possible after the company is requested to proceed by the President of the commercial court.





+*Filing with the Trade and Company Registry*+

Whereas both financials approval and filing steps are mandatory under French law, some companies decide not to file their accounts without immediate and serious consequence (in case they receive an injunction from the Commercial court to file their accounts, they will have a some time to proceed). 

+FR CM would prefer not to file financials and so far we did not file them to preserve confidentiality+.

If in the future we will opt for filing then, we need to grant powers of attorney to local law firm (eg OC FR) for them to assist with filing.







+*Statutory Auditor and Management Report*+ 

At the end of each financial year, it is required to check whether the company has reached 2 of the 3 below thresholds and if so it must appoint a Statutory Auditor and it should prepare a management report for the accounts approval.

_Thresholds :_

_(i) turnover of 8 million Euros,_ 

_(ii) total balance sheet of 4 million Euros net_ 

_(iii) 50 employees average across the FY_

This sounds like a problem, not  because of potential litigation, but more due to the risk to our reputation and the broader negative impact on society.

As a platform operator, we cannot be held liable since we are neither a seller nor a deliverer of alcohol. According to the Alcohol Act, the responsibility lies with the seller. 

~_§ 45.  Measures to ensure order and security_~
 ~_(1) It is prohibited to sell alcoholic beverages to persons exhibiting signs of intoxication._~

 ~_(2) A seller shall not knowingly serve any persons who buy alcoholic beverages for the purpose of offering or handing the alcoholic beverages over to persons exhibiting signs of intoxication._~

However, in online sales, where sellers can't reasonably assess the condition of the person ordering alcohol, the liability shifts to the courier who delivers it.

Despite this, there are actions we can take to regulate the situation and demonstrate our social responsibility. Here are some immediate steps we can take:

# Communicate clearly to couriers that delivering alcohol to intoxicated individuals is strictly prohibited. Violations could result in suspension from the Bolt Food platform and potential administrative liability (up to EUR 1000 for a natural person, up to EUR 3000 for a legal person).
# Enable couriers to cancel a client's order, and ensure the client isn't charged for the alcohol if, upon handling the alcohol, the courier discovers that the person is already drunk. Is this technically possible? 
# Implement temporary suspension for the first violation (per clause 9.1 of T&C for couriers), and for repeated offenses, consider permanent suspension (per clause 4.7 of T&C for couriers)

Dear Sir/Madam,

Thank you for bringing this matter to our attention. We appreciate your concerns and are committed to addressing the issue to the best of our ability.

Please be informed that Bolt operates as a platform, acting as a marketplace connecting restaurants/stores (sellers), eaters, and independent couriers. Bolt neither acts as a seller of alcohol nor as a provider of delivery services to eaters.

Couriers utilize Bolt's services for the provision of delivery services through the Bolt Food application in their independent capacity (as independent service providers). As Bolt does not employ couriers, our legal authority to directly supervise their actions is limited, and our influence over their conduct is constrained. Consequently, Bolt cannot be held responsible for the handling of alcohol by couriers for intoxicated individuals.

However, we are committed to addressing the issue within the scope of our platform operator role.

To mitigate the problem:

(i) We will issue informative notices to all couriers, explicitly stating that delivering alcohol to intoxicated individuals is strictly prohibited. Violating this policy could result in suspension from the Bolt Food platform and potential administrative consequences.

(ii) We will take swift action by suspending any couriers from the Bolt Food platform reported for delivering alcohol to intoxicated people. 

We trust that these measures will contribute to a safer and more responsible delivery service. If you have any further questions or concerns, please feel free to reach out to us at [*email*].

Best regards, 

Bolt Food Team

Hello! 

I see why the other contracting parties are opposing clause 10.2.1., subrogation of the claim (in case of liability) is a completely normal business practice. 

Generally speaking, when it comes to lease agreements, two types of insurance are relevant: property insurance and liability insurance. 

Property insurance is to secure any risks related fire, flooding, theft, vandalism, other natural causes, etc. This insurance should be bought by the party who has an insurable interest, i.e. the owner of the property, i.e. the landlord/lessor. Often, landlords try to push this on us but we should object. (In this contract, this type of insurane is referenced in 10.1.)

Liability insurance is to secure any damage we might cause to the property, to its neighbouring properties, or to other third parties. That is - a fire caused by our batteries (most common), or us damaging the property with our machinery and other operations. This type of policy we have already in place across Europe. (In this contract, it’s referenced in 10.5.) 

Now, coming back to 10.2.1.

# If there is a flooding for example, then the damage to the property shall be protected by the property insurance bought by the landlord according to 10.1. And in this case, subrogation is not possible anyway, because we are not liable for that damage. 
# However, if the warehouse catches on fire due to our batteries, then the damage to the property shall be covered by the general liability policy that we buy according to 10.5. If the landlord happens to claim any damage from our fire under his insurance policy (the 10.1 policy), then his insurer will have the subrogation right from our general liability policy (the 10.5. policy). 

This is all common business practice, and it’s completely normal to subrogate a claim in case of our liability. Hope this helps to understand why the other party wishes to remove 10.2.1, and why it’s normal. 



On another note, I see from 10.5. that we will be taking on an obligation to insure our (movable) property inside the warehouse (this is called assets insurance). For context, Bolt does not usually buy assets insurance (apart from a few dark stores), as it has been the business decision, to assume the risks on our own. So currently, we are not compliant with that part of 10.5. If assets insurance is required (although we can probably negotiate on that term, as why would the landlord care whether we have insured our own property or not) or something we wish to buy here, please, let me know, and I can obtain quotes. 



Best 

Karmel

*Here are the queries that have been run:*

To get a list of all orders starting from {{2023-12-01}} which have discrepancy between authorization and captured amounts.

{code:sql}SELECT booking.created_date, adjustment_amount_total, booking_amount_total, capture_amount_total, target_account_id as user_id FROM ng_balance_user.balance_user_booking booking
                  JOIN ng_balance_user.balance_user_booking_item booking_item ON booking_item.booking_id = booking.id
                  JOIn ng_balance_user.balance_user_billing_transaction trx ON trx.id = booking.transaction_id
WHERE booking.created_date > date '2023-12-01'
  AND booking_item.created_date > date '2023-12-01'
  AND trx.created_date > date '2023-12-01'
  AND source_type = 'delivery'
  AND booking_item.booked_amount < booking_item.captured_amount;{code}

Here is the query to get campaign for food from the {{taxify_delivery_basket}} side.

{code:sql}select campaign.price_after_discount, campaign.price_before_discount, campaign.id, campaign.user_basket_id  from master_basket
join user_basket on user_basket.master_basket_id = master_basket.id
join campaign on campaign.user_basket_id = user_basket.id
# join campaign_item on campaign_item.campaign_id = campaign.id
where master_basket.order_id = <<<ORDER ID HERE>>> and campaign.target = 'item_price';{code}

Here is the query to get campaign for food from the {{taxify_delivery_order}} side.

{code:sql}select campaign.price_before_discount, campaign.price_after_discount, campaign.order_user_basket_id, campaign.id from `order`
join user_basket on user_basket.order_id = `order`.id
join campaign on campaign.order_user_basket_id = user_basket.id
where `order`.id = 149708229 and campaign.target = 'item_price';{code}

Exmo. Dr. Gil Valente Maia,

Acusamos recepção da V/comunicação relativa ao V/Constituinte Pedro Daniel Azevedo Monteiro.

Cumpre-nos informar que os termos e condições aceites pelo Operador de TVDE ao serviço do qual o Sr. Pedro Monteiro presta serviços de transportes na plataforma Bolt determinam que:

“ _4.8. O Operador TVDE não deve envolver-se com ou permitir qualquer comportamento fraudulento na Plataforma Bolt em associação com a sua conta. Qualquer comportamento fraudulento em associação com a conta do Operador TVDE causado ou permitido por um Motorista que atue em sua representação será considerado uma violação material do presente Contrato pelo Operador TVDE.”_

_“18.5. Tendo em conta que a Bolt é solidariamente responsável pelo cumprimento das obrigações decorrentes do Contrato de Serviços de Transporte (nos termos impostos pela Lei nº. 45/2018, de 10 de agosto), as seguintes violações por parte do Operador TVDE serão consideradas razões imperativas para a rescisão imediata: (i) empréstimo não autorizado de uma Conta Bolt ou outro comportamento fraudulento.”_

A decisão de suspender a conta do Sr. Pedro Monteiro associada à conta do Operador de TVDE do mesmo na plataforma foi tomada pelo facto das seguintes disposições dos termos e condições aceites pelo Operador de TVDE não estarem a ser cumpridas

_“1.10. É responsabilidade do Operador TVDE assegurar que todos os Motoristas que prestem Serviços de Transporte em sua representação devem ser aptos e encontrar-se devidamente certificados nos termos da legislação aplicável para o acesso e exercício da profissão de motorista de TVDE(...).”_

_“2.6 (...) Os Motoristas que atuem em sua representação terão acesso à Plataforma Bolt em associação com a Conta de Operador TVDE do Operador TVDE. Os dados de login para os Motoristas são pessoais para cada indivíduo. Por razões de segurança e compliance, o Operador TVDE não deve permitir que qualquer pessoa utilize uma Conta de Motorista pessoal que não lhe pertença. A Bolt não proíbe o Operador TVDE de permitir que qualquer Motorista individual que atue em sua representação subcontrate os Serviços de Transporte, contanto que todos os requisitos legais sejam cumpridos e que tal subcontratante se registe na Plataforma Bolt como um Motorista do Operador TVDE.”_

Concretamente, os dados técnicos indicam que, durante o período em que a verificação de identidade foi efectuada, dois aparelhos diferentes estavam ligados à conta de motorista.

Acresce, que de acordo com a  Lei n.º 45/2018 de 10 de agosto que estabelece o regime jurídico da atividade de transporte individual e remunerado de passageiros em veículos descaracterizados a partir de plataforma electrónica, apenas podem conduzir veículos de TVDE os motoristas inscritos junto de plataforma eletrónica, devendo os mesmos cumprir todos os requisitos estabelecidos no artigo 10 desta lei. Em conformidade, o artigo 14(2) desta lei impõe à Bolt enquanto operador de plataforma eletrónica o dever de bloqueio do acesso aos serviços prestados pela mesma por parte de motoristas que incumpram qualquer dos requisitos legais impostos.

Deste modo, mantemos a decisão de suspensão da conta do Sr. Pedro Monteiro associada à conta do Operador de TVDE do mesmo, considerando estar a mesma em conformidade com os nossos procedimentos internos, bem como os termos e condições e legislação aplicáveis.

To better illustrate exactly how the scheme works: 

* The couriers place themselves on the map, using an app, at a location where they will receive inflated earnings (in these most recent case, right after an exit on a major road with a few exits)
* They “Accept” the order from that location according to our GPS data, but are actually in a provider dense area, where they will likely receive orders from
* The GPS track then jumps to their actual location, where the signal is clear afterwards, following their actual route

Hi [~accountid:63184a39316bbc56c425dacf] ,

If it’s not possible to implement the requested solution, an alternate I could think of is to have a fixed % for deduction of  meal provided to employees during their trips.

Typically, we could use our group policy reference where the deduction rate of meal provided are 20% for breakfast, 40% for lunch and 40% for dinner (if local legislation does not state anything explicitly). 

So the total daily rate of allowance should be pro-rated based on hours spent in the trip on a single date (based on departure and arrival time) and then adjusted (reduced) by the deduction rate for the meals provided. Similar solution what we intended to implement in UK previously.

So using the same example [~accountid:637f785b9341d1f13605b0be]  previously used, 


*Samples:*
Business trip to Belgium 20 h. Basic rate is 50 EUR.

# No meals provided: 50 EUR
# Breakfast provided: Employee will get Basic rate minus 25%. 

50-12,5 = 37,5 EUR. 

# Breakfast + dinner provided: Employee will get Basic rate minus 25% and 25%. 50-12,5-12,5 = 25 EUR



*If we implement alternate solution:*


Business trip to Belgium 20 h. Basic rate is 50 EUR.

# No meals provided: 50 EUR
# Breakfast provided: Employee will get Basic rate minus 20%, (50*.80) 40 EUR.
# Breakfast + dinner provided: Employee will get Basic rate minus 20% (breakfast) and 40% (Dinner). 50-10-20) = 20 EUR


However, [~accountid:61e58b98fd5a690068b1dc22] , implementing solution like this could contradict with CZ local legislation, which dictates companies are at discretion to reduce the prescribed rate at max by 25%  of the expected payment employees are to receive for eligible business trips. If the employer were to provide anything above this limit, such an increase would have to be considered as the taxable income of the employee, which is not a desirable solution for us. Hence, you should do further risk assessment and propose a fixed rate of deductions for the meals provided.

*Warm Regards,*
Subarna

* Will informing riders (i.e. having stickers in cars) be a prerequisite of having CCTV?
** {color:#bf2600}Stickers will be provided together with the device by the selected partner (Matrix IQ) and fitted as part of the installation process. This is also one of the requirements of the private hire vehicle licence that the driver/vehicle proprietor needs to adhere to. Licensing authorities in the UK require a specific sticker that includes the name and contact details of the Data Controller and we are working together with the partner to make sure correct signage is distributed.{color}
* Will we inform the drivers that it’s their responsibility to respond to riders re their privacy rights? 
** {color:#bf2600}Yes, the partner will educate drivers on their responsibilities. We will collaborate with the partner on creating this educational material and also include a Q&A on the website where we will be introducing the offer. {color}



As to your point on *user requests channeled to Bolt* - as many drivers in the UK are already using CCTV, I checked how local authorities approach this within their published CCTV policies - example from Wolverhampton council guidelines below:

* If a passenger or any other individual wants to request CCTV footage relating to themself, they should make a Subject Access Request (SAR) to the Data Controller detailed on the signage in the vehicle. Information on how to make a valid SAR is available at [https://ico.org.uk/your-data-matters/your-right-toget-copies-of-your-data/|https://ico.org.uk/your-data-matters/your-right-toget-copies-of-your-data/] 
* If a passenger has an issue with their taxi journey relating to the use of CCTV they should contact the Data Controller, in the first instance, using the details displayed on the CCTV signage within the vehicle. If the Data Controller fails to resolve the issue, the complainant may escalate this to the ICO at [https://ico.org.uk/make-a-complaint/|https://ico.org.uk/make-a-complaint/|smart-link]  

I suggest we prepare a similar response, stating that Bolt doesn’t have any access to the recordings and that the request must go to the data controller. If the rider escalates the issue further or requests the details of the driver because they failed to note the data controller details from the vehicle signage we can

* Offer to try reaching out to the driver and see if they consent to share the data controller details (as stated on the vehicle signage) retrospectively with the rider (and share the data only if we have written consent from the driver). 
* note that if their request concerns a safety incident, we suggest contacting the Police.

What we are trying to do here is to avoid any incident with scooters in uninsured markets being escalated to your team just because we do not have insurance, nor procedures to deal with them. 

Right now, procedures and templates are based on the fact that we have insurance, and if the insurance does not cover it, we have an “escalation to legal” process. 

What we would need to do is:

* Reviewing the current templates and see whether they can be adapted to uninsured markets
* Check whether the “escalation to legal” process is fine for uninsured markets, to avoid your team being overwhelmed. 
** Keep in mind that usually when Bolt compensates a user, it’s also based on the local team’s decision. 

----

Our current templates are: 

*Third-party demanding payment for injury or property damage from an uninsured user (user broke T&C)*

_Bolt has several measures in place to prevent and/or mitigate the impact of loss or damage to third parties._ {color:#bf2600}_This includes taking out a policy of third-party liability insurance on behalf of our users when using our e-vehicles, as long as they adhere to our terms and conditions._{color}

{color:#bf2600}_Unfortunately, in your case, we have been informed that our insurer will not cover this incident because the Bolt user responsible for the incident was in breach of Bolt T&Cs._{color}

_Upon reviewing your claim and the available evidence, we find that Bolt's responsibility for the alleged damages has not been established. Therefore, we cannot assume liability and we are unable to fulfill your request for compensation. In such situations, the e-vehicle rider is responsible for their actions and any resulting damage while operating the e-vehicle._
_We recommend contacting your insurance company to seek coverage for the damages. While we are unable to assist further with this specific request, we apologise for any inconvenience and trust you will understand our position on this matter._

*Uninsured user (user broke T&C) demanding payment for injury or property damage due to an accident with a third party*

_We're sorry to hear about your recent incident involving a Bolt e-vehicle. We also understand you're seeking compensation._

_Bolt has several measures in place to prevent and/or mitigate the impact of loss or damage in the event of an accident._ {color:#bf2600}_This includes taking out a policy of insurance on behalf of our users when using our e-vehicles, as long as they adhere to our terms and conditions._{color}

{color:#bf2600}_Upon reviewing your claim and the evidence, we find that you acted in breach of our Riding Rules and violated our general terms and conditions. As such, our insurer will not cover this incident, nor will Bolt accept liability for the loss or damages._{color}

_You may wish to explore claiming the damages suffered from your insurance company and we are afraid that we are not in a position to assist you further with this particular request._

_Once again, we are sorry for the inconvenience and trust that you will understand our position._

----

h3. Contacting the Legal Team

A [ServiceDesk Ticket|https://taxify.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/47/group/169/create/787] to the Legal team should be created
*if:*

* A reported incident isn’t liable for insurance, or
* The insurance claim was rejected

*And:*

* We are contacted by a lawyer, or
* The reporting party provides clear evidence that a Bolt rental was at fault, or
* The case is particularly sensitive (example: a third-party with vision impairment falls over a badly parked scooter).

Make sure to include:

* A copy of the formal rejection letter from insurers (if applicable);
* A formal demand from the customer outlining their demands for compensation;
* Evidence they can provide to substantiate their claim; and

In addition:

* Escalate the case to your TL or POC
* If perceived as a potential crisis, the TL can share the case in the relevant markets crisis channel for further input from other stakeholders.

*Section 2* 

Anybody holding a written document that can be assumed to be of importance as evidence is obliged to produce it; in criminal cases, however, such an obligation is not imposed upon the suspect or any person related to him as stated in Chapter 36, Section 3. Neither a public official nor any other person referred to in Chapter 36, Section 5, may produce a written document if it can be assumed that its contents is such that he may not be heard as a witness thereto; when the document is held by the party for whose benefit an obligation of confidentiality is imposed, that party is not obliged to produce the document. Since there’s no insurance in place (nor is it mandatory), this issue, ipso facto, is not a matter of insurance. I see it as a matter of liability.

I guess the questions here are (including, but not limited to), is Bolt liable for

* damage caused to third-parties by parked scooters
* damage caused to riders by accidents
* damage caused to riders by malfunctioning scooters
* damage caused to third-parties by riders in an accident 
* damage caused to third-parties by riders involving a malfunctioning scooter
* damage cause to third-parties by riders whilst in breach of our T&Cs. 

There are many markets where Bolt merely rejects liability (due to the liability falling on the rider, or other factors), using prepared templates. However, there are also markets where Bolt is jointly and severally liable for the damage. Or Bolt is liable for parked scooters merely as being the owner/operator of these scooters. 

When safety agents receive a ticket with a claim for damages: a) they escalate to insurance, b) reject the claim, or c) escalate to legal (if liability cannot be rejected).

Seeing as the step a) is currently skipped here. We jump immediately to steps b) and c). So what, I believe, Alessandro is seeking is to know whether we can use the templates where we reject the claim, or if we need to modify the templates.

In general, accidents that are (supposedly) caused by malfunctioning scooters, are not covered, as according to our T&C’s the rider takes on the obligation to make sure that the condition of the scooter is suitable for a trip. 

Not sure how a “flat battery” would be handled here - whether it is a malfunction or not. In my personal experience, when Bolt scooter’s battery is running low or flat, the scooter gets really low first and then eventually stops moving. So hard to imagine someone ending up in a serious accident due to low battery - unless it’s a malfunction (not a standard flat battery situation). 

!Screenshot 2024-02-02 at 16.05.10.png|width=797,height=550!

I see from a deepl translation of the claim, that indeed, it might be a malfunctioning scooter, actually.

Considering this, I think local ops should dive into the scooter data - i.e. was the low battery status registered in our logs, were there any complaints submitted about the scooter, and did the scooter go to service after this trip? 

If we have sufficient proof, that the rider did not fall due to a malfunctioning scooter, we can try to escalate this to our insurer (as often people tend to blame our scooters if they get hurt on their own.) 

However, is there any actual injury to the rider - or is it merely “phobia” as suggested by the deepl translation? 

Our insurance covers death and permanent disability, and I don’t think they will consider this “phobia” as a permanent disability.

Please note that all special clauses should be listed in the Special Terms rather than amended in the General Terms.

clause 3: "Clientul va efectua plata conform facturii fiscale în termen de 15 zile de la data la care factura corespunzatoare a fost recepționată in original de către Client." - If the meaning of the new wording is that we must send the paper copy of the invoice then we should probably avoid this.
clauses 4.1, 4.2, 4.3, 4.4 and 4.5 - Please push back on these. These clauses attempt to extend Bolt's liability, which is hard no for us. If the customer is not satisfied with our service they are free to terminate the agreement by giving 7 days' prior written notice.
new clause 7.1 - this is fine to accept.
new clause 7.2 - this is fine to accept.
new clause 7.3 - this is fine to accept.
clause 6.6.1 - cannot agree to 6.6.1 as we will not generally extend our liability and this wording would contradict clause 6.4.
clause 6.9 - let's push back on this. I don't think this is so critical service for them that they want to regulate everything. Parties can terminate the agreement by giving 7 days notice, so the risk for the customer should be quite low.
clause 6.12 - I would not add this wording as "assumed obligations" creates more risk. The right to claim damages in case of a breach of contract are provided by default.
7.3 - please push back on this. Breach of a contract can happen and parties can resolve this amicably. Otherwise, the other party can terminate by giving 7 days' prior written notice. If, however, the breach is material, then termination can be done without the need to wait for 7 days. It would be unfair to allow to terminate the agreement immediately without a material breach. They can specify what material breach is for them in case they want to ensure that they can terminate the agreement in case there is a breach of specific clauses that they are concerned about. For example, we can add the wording that the parties consider as a material breach of the contract if the party breaches it's obligations under clauses 7.1 and 7.2.
7.4 - I do not recommend accepting this wording, but this is purely monetary risk and is subject to business decision. Bolt may lose money in case something happens due to customer or it's users, but the claim is brought after the agreement is terminated.
clause 8.3 - please push back on this and explain that Bolt has right to amend General Terms from time to time unilaterally and will notify the customer about it 30 days in advance. However, Bolt may not amend Special Terms without customer's consent.
clause 8.10 - we can add this, but I am not sure how we will check this.
clause 8.11 - this clause is not entirely clear, but probably ok to add if they can explain what they mean by it. I.e. what are the benefits, losses and what means interference with the operations.

*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 



Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *8/11/2023.*



After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 



As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software. Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail,  we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

*Personal Data we collect about you from other sources*
*Background Check Data*

We collect personal data about you after you submit your sign up application in order to check you meet the relevant local conditions to use the Bolt Services, including:

* data about criminal convictions and offences, where permitted under local laws and regulations
* driver history
* license status
* prior addresses
* permits issued by the Government or official authority to operate as a transportation services provider in the United Kingdom

We also use the data you submit to screen you in relation to sanctions and anti-money laundering. This information may also be collected by an authorised third party vendor on our behalf.



*Driver Compliance Data*
We collect personal data from service providers that conduct vehicle and driver compliance checks including car insurance and status, liability insurance (if applicable), registrations, certifications and other documentation that are required in the applicable jurisdiction for providing the transportation services, and also screenshots of public databases supporting that we conducted a compliance check, after you submit your sign up application in order to start using the Bolt services,  in order to verify any information you supplied to Bolt during registration.



*Third Party Programs Data*
We collect information about your participation in third-party programs that provide financial instruments, such as insurance, payments, or benefits such as pension at privileged pricing.

* Name

Here are the legal grounds (known as a *'legal basis'*) under data protection law:

* *Performance of a Contract:* When it is necessary for Bolt (or a third party) to process your personal data to provide you with the services we promised you and to meet our obligations under our Terms and Conditions for Drivers.



* *Legitimate Interests:* We may process your personal data relying on legitimate interest grounds. In countries where legitimate interest is not an available lawful basis for Bolt’s processing activities, we will instead rely on an alternative valid legal basis.



* *Consent:* When we ask you to actively indicate your agreement to our use of your personal data for a certain purpose of which you have been fully informed. ​​Where we rely on consent to process your personal data, you can withdraw your consent to such activities at any time. Withdrawal of the consent does not affect the lawfulness of prior processing. In countries where soft opt-in is not an available lawful basis for Bolt’s processing activities, we will instead rely on an alternative valid legal basis.



* *Compliance with Legal Obligations:* When we must process your personal data to comply with a law or regulation in the markets we operate in, such as to comply with our licensing conditions and our obligations under tax and accounting laws.

Hello, [~accountid:60528922695c3900706cc77c], please see my comments:

*1)Question:* Can we actually block them based on this third party’s report? We don’t really have any evidence and the report is not coming from an actual witness, where we could take these reports as confirmed to have occurred.

*Comments:* Who could be these third parties? I assume these could only be witnesses who have seen a courier handling alcohol to a drunk person, for example, family members. I advise gradually increasing the intensity of our response from mild to more restrictive. 

# If we receive any complaint, first, we  *educate couriers* that providing alcohol to drunk people is forbidden, inform them how to act in this case (contact CS) and what are the consequences – administrative liability, as well as suspension
# If education does not work, and we receive a repetitive complaint we  *temporarily suspend a courier* for a few days, providing (i) clear advanced information and (ii) reasons for such a suspension. Temporary suspension is regulated by clause 9.1 of T&C (in this case the reason is a breach of applicable laws (Alcohol Act) and damage to Bolt's brand and reputation).
# After temporary suspension, we  *give a courier one more chance* to improve his/her performance. 
If it does not work and more complaints are received, only then under clause 4.7 we may  *permanently block* him/her by providing (i) a clear advance notice, (ii) reasoning and (iii) information that the courier has the right to challenge his/her termination under clause 14.2 of the [T&C for couriers.|https://assets.ctfassets.net/tk7rwcciwvbq/4TC5ah75KrZSkpkzd5nBp6/9ef85b3d18b4e16f294391dffbd20d82/V5_of_Bolt-Courier_T_C__LT__-ENG-.pdf] 
## As a general rule, we can permanently block couriers only by giving notice at least 30 days in advance (clause 9.2). 
## The only exception that allows Bolt to terminate a courier without a 30-day notice is when a courier *repeatedly* breaches or fails to comply with any of the obligations set out in T&C (clause 4.4”c” of Regulation (EU) 2019/1150. This means that a courier shall be given a chance to improve his/her behaviour at least 2 times before we permanently block him/her claiming repetitive breach of rules.

*2) Question:*  Can we also permanently block the eater’s account based on the third party’s report, although it’s not confirmed by the eater themselves?

*Comments:* Why should we block an eater in this case? To my knowledge, there is no law mandating a consumer not to order alcohol if he/she is drunk.

7.2 clause of T&C for clients states that _“Bolt is entitled_ +_to remove a Client_+ _from the Bolt Food Platform_ +_with immediate effect and/or refuse or cancel any Orders, if the Client causes any abuse or harm to the Bolt Food Platform_+_, if Bolt has reasonable belief of fraudulent acts by the Client when using the Bolt Food Platform, or if the Client otherwise fails to comply with his/her obligations under these General Terms_*_”._* 

In the event of repeated complaints where a specific user being drunk orders alcohol, we may suspend him/her only from the option to order alcohol via Bolt Food app for his/her safety and to protect Bolt's reputation. The decision shall be communicated to the client informing about the reasons behind this decision. 

*3)  Question:* Couriers cannot cancel the order, and we instruct them to contact CS in cases where alcohol delivery is not possible (this also includes cases of underage eaters, or those unable to produce an ID), who can then cancel the order and refund the eater for the delivery. Is that a feasible solution?

*Comments:* Yes, in this case, a courier shall contact the CS, provide reasoning and ask to cancel the alcohol order and refund the eater. Does it mean that the whole order will be cancelled (if a person ordered other goods besides alco) or only alco? It is preferred to cancel only the alcohol order and keep the rest.

{color:#008da6}*All that I clarified with Privacy team / have to update in the process map:*{color}

* The escalation should be: Tier2 -> CS Privacy Compliance team -> Privacy Legal Team? And Tier2 should not reach out directly to Privacy Legal Team?
** yes, correct, the idea is that Tier 2 should not directly escalate to us. CS Privacy takes on this responsibility for escalating to us. However, we need to agree with Lisanna on this whether it's reasonable
* If the request is escalated by Tier 2 *after one month from the date of the receipt*, investigate the reason and escalate it to Privacy Legal Team *for their instructions*
* What CS Privacy Compliance agent should do if: 1-The acknowledgment letter wasn't sent to the user, 2-The acknowledgment letter was sent with the wrong date
** 1-ask Tier 2 to immediately send it, 2 - leave it "as is" and remind to Tier 2 to calculate one month correctly
* Access request → The user who is requesting their data has an account that is deleted → Verify that the state of the account: deleted, blocked, or moved to another fleet - *applicable to all user types*
* Inform Privacy Legal Team in SD once the response is sent to the user - *NOT NEEDED*
* Verify that no *-specific-* other questions related to  their data are asked by the user
* Edit all *erasure request* part
* *Rectification -* 
** if agent can edit the data (e.g. Rider is asking to edit their name in Bolt app) then agent should follow the specific instructions (we will add links to processes). But if agent can't edit the data or is unsure about the accuracy, then this instruction should be followed
** *Address the concerns of the agent in the internal note* and ask the agent to proceed with further steps in the process
** *If these concerns cannot be addressed by you,* escalate the case to the Privacy
* *Portability* - The reason we added it like this is that access and portability are quite similar, but from the privacy side we are entitled to share a limited info under the GDPR. We have to make sure that agents re-approve with the users whether it's a transfer or access request.
* *Withdraw consent* - 
** If the user asks to withdraw their consent in the request, it means they want to revoke the permission they previously gave to Bolt for processing some of their personal data. This can include consent for sharing their phone number with the driver or rider, age verification, driver sign-up, and other purposes.
** if for some reason more than 12hrs passed from receiving the request - Still escalate to CS Privacy Comp team, but CS Privacy Comp should ensure they address this quickly
** If the user does not respond within 24 hours / If it’s clearly stated, escalate the case to the Privacy for further processing and *await their instructions*.
* *Objection request* - this part will be updated as it was missed when transferring from G Doc to Beehive for Tier 2 agents

Queries:

*Get CPA polygon*

{noformat}with poly as (
	select 
		concat(
			'POLYGON((',
			array_join(
				transform(
					split(snap_polygon, ','),
					e -> array_join(reverse(split(e, ' ')), ' ')
				),
				','
			),
			'))'
		) as poly_wkt
	from ng_public.smart_pickups_area
	where name = 'Poiana Brasov Cable Car'
	and city_id = 802
)
select
	geometry_as_geojson(ST_Polygon(poly_wkt)) original_poly,
	geometry_as_geojson(ST_Buffer(ST_Polygon(poly_wkt), 0.0003)) as buffered_poly
from poly;{noformat}

*First time order stats with exact CPA polygon*

{noformat}with poly as (
	select 
		concat(
			'POLYGON((',
			array_join(
				transform(
					split(snap_polygon, ','),
					e -> array_join(reverse(split(e, ' ')), ' ')
				),
				','
			),
			'))'
		) as poly_wkt
	from ng_public.smart_pickups_area
	where name = 'Poiana Brasov Cable Car'
	and city_id = 802
),
first_time_orders as (
	select
		date_trunc('month', co.created) as month,
		ST_Intersects(ST_Point(co.lng, co.lat), (select ST_Polygon(poly_wkt) from poly)) as is_in_cpa
	FROM ng_public.company_order as co
	INNER JOIN ng_public.company_order_try as cot
	    ON co.id = cot.order_id and co.city_id = cot.city_id
	LEFT JOIN ng_public.etl_first_finished_ride_for_user as first_ride
	    ON first_ride.order_id = cot.order_id AND first_ride.city_id = cot.city_id AND first_ride.created_date >= DATE '2022-06-30'
	WHERE
	    cot.state = 'finished'
	    and cot.retry_to_try is null
	    and co.created_date between DATE '2023-01-01' and DATE '2024-01-01'
	    and cot.created_date between DATE '2023-01-01' and DATE '2024-01-01'
	    and first_ride.user_id IS NOT NULL
	    and co.city_id = 802 and cot.city_id = 802 and first_ride.city_id = 802
)
select month, count(*) as first_time_orders from first_time_orders
where is_in_cpa
group by 1
order by month;{noformat}

*First time order stats with buffered polygon*

	select

			'POLYGON((',

				transform(
					split(snap_polygon, ','),

				),

			'))'

	from ng_public.smart_pickups_area
	where name = 'Poiana Brasov Cable Car'

),
first_time_orders as (

	FROM ng_public.company_order as co
	INNER JOIN ng_public.company_order_try as cot

The issuer name on the invoice depends on the invoicing strategy specified in the fee calculator (communicated to Billing team by local team).

Invoicing strategy “Company” means the issuer is the legal entity (often a fleet). For this driver, it’s ‘Driver’ because this is a fleet you are using for private drivers in this city. 

If he wants the invoice issuer to be an entity, then you should create a fleet profile in Admin for this fleet and add him under this fleet. Or if he is an employee of an existing fleet, you can just add him there. The invoicing strategy should be ‘Company’ for this fleet. And Billing Information in his profile should also reflect the company details.

{{Background:}}

1] The problem was identified by [~accountid:5d6e089134b3d20d9777ef90] from MarTech in this ticket.

As, if we are prompted to receive consent by the gatekeepers, it would make sense to convert to GDPR consent for this as well.

3] Me and [@anton.hmelnitski|https://taxify.slack.com/team/UMKNTHN4S] are currently working on understanding the requirements for consent collection triggered by the DMA. Anton is clarifying Google and other similar gatekeeper requirements.

4] The change, if implemented, would be substantial - only under the DMA scope, we will have to collect consent for some important targeted advertisement activities with gatekeepers - Google, Meta, probably TikTok, etc. As it makes sense to expand the scope and implement this change together with the requirements under the ePrivacy Directive, the majority of our in-app analytics (advertisement&functional) will have to be converted to consent-based.

{{As for the help from product legal, we would really appreciate the following:}}

    reg_number,

FROM (
         SELECT
             dsc.driver_id, dsc.car_id, c.reg_number, dsc.start, dsc.end
         FROM taxify_fleet.driver_selected_car dsc
                  JOIN taxify_fleet.car c ON c.id = dsc.car_id
         WHERE dsc.end IS NULL
           AND dsc.start <= CONVERT_TZ('2024-01-28 23:59:59', 'Europe/London', 'UTC')
           AND dsc.driver_id IN (${driverIds})

         UNION

         SELECT
             dsc.driver_id, dsc.car_id, c.reg_number, dsc.start, dsc.end
         FROM taxify_fleet.driver_selected_car dsc
                  JOIN taxify_fleet.car c ON c.id = dsc.car_id
         WHERE dsc.end >= CONVERT_TZ('2024-01-22 00:00', 'Europe/London', 'UTC')
           AND dsc.start <= CONVERT_TZ('2024-01-28 23:59:59', 'Europe/London', 'UTC')
           AND dsc.driver_id IN (${driverIds})
     ) selected_cars
ORDER BY driver_id ASC, -end DESC;{noformat}

*Risk to Brussels and Oslo licenses*: We should treat commitments made in each tender bid as binding. Bolt's failure to meet these commitments risks license revocation by the city or a competitor's challenge. Bolt is already in breach of the Brussels license conditions. 

* While immediate license revocation is possible, it is unlikely. If we adopt a reactive stance, we might expect a competitor complaint, a city query, a chance to respond, and a rectification notice. 
* An alternative strategy may be for PP to proactively engage with each city, stating the problem and outlining Bolt’s compliance plan. The level of competitor compliance is relevant to this discussion.
* It’s also important to note that Oslo and Brussels have discretion in whether or not to strictly enforce license obligations. 

*Dummy cameras:* The deployment of dummy cameras or empty housings is high risk. It is likely to be viewed as deliberate, deceptive conduct to misrepresent the capability/safety/compliance level of Bolt’s fleet. 

* Risk materialization is high: competitor scrutiny, user/third party injuries, privacy/data requests, vandalism, internal leaks
* Potential impact is also high: 
** Distinct from failing to fulfill the commitments in each tender bid, deliberate misrepresentations constitute a fundamental *_breach of contract_* (immediate loss of license, regulatory penalties, future application bars)
** *_Consumer law, Product Safety and Product Liability_* (if a user/pedestrian is harmed because a product does not perform as safely as represented, product liability claims arise. Intentional misconduct gives rise to additional punitive damages.)
** *_Personal injury and insurance claims_* (if a user/pedestrian is seriously injured, Bolt’s safety features may be closely scrutinized. Purposeful misrepresentations regarding safety features attract additional liability. Engaging in misleading practices can lead insurers to increase premiums, exclude coverage and increase scrutiny of future claims)

Non-legal, PR risk: Discovery of fake cameras or empty housings presents a large PR risk. Any decisions taken on this issue need to be convincingly and logically explainable to the city, a court or the media. 

*Recommendation:* adopt a compliance plan that satisfactorily meets the promises made in each tender bid or acknowledge the risk that partial compliance may result in either license being challenged or revoked.

Hey Peerasorn ,

In order to create base fee calculators, we would need the following information per city:

* *Commission rate*: Commission percentage that will apply per ride to the driver/fleet.
* *Invoicing strategy*: Driver or Company. This will define to whom payouts will go, and invoices will be issued.
* *Booking fee:* Is there an active booking fee in the city? If so, do you want it to be deducted from the driver (and reflected on the commission invoice), or be a 100% driver income?
* *Cash-blocking thresholds*: Defines the cash ride limits for blocking/unblocking cash rides for a driver. This can be copied from other cities, but please discuss with [{color:#b3f5ff}Billing Analytics{color}|https://taxify.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/3/group/1240/create/806] if your market is cash-heavy.
** Max negative balance before messaging: The threshold where we will notify the driver that they are getting closer to being cash-blocked
** Max negative balance before removing cash payments: The debt threshold we allow cash rides up to. After the driver exceeds this threshold, cash orders will be disabled.
** Minimal balance to unblock cash rides: The balance threshold where we will once again unblock the driver’s cash rides.
* *List of company_ids you want this fee calculator to be attached to*.

It is a default fee calculator template created by Billing team in order for local operations teams to easily attach the relevant fee calculator to new companies. [Please read this guide to see how|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/1603928517/Base+fee+calculators].

Detailed id calculation:

{noformat}# 1. find finished orders from about 95d ago, get 'id' of their price lock

select pl.id, pl.created
from final f
         JOIN taxify_pricing_order.price_lock pl on f.city_id = pl.city_id AND f.order_id = pl.order_id
where f.created < DATE_SUB(NOW(), INTERVAL 95 DAY)
order by f.created desc
limit 2;

# result: id,created
# 4004533069,2023-11-03 10:55:51
# 4004551379,2023-11-03 10:59:59


# 2. check that price_lock ids from this range have unfinished orders and are indeed incrementing:

select pl.id, pl.created, f.order_id
from price_lock pl
         LEFT JOIN taxify_pricing_order.final f on pl.city_id = f.city_id AND f.order_id = pl.order_id
where f.id IS NULL AND pl.id < 4004533069
order by pl.id desc
limit 10

# round the ID{noformat}

Shared feedback with Abhinav and Dmitri Suholet: 

* In the EU, there are strict rules against imposing card processing fees and displaying pricing information in such a way that it is “hidden“
* Pricing information must always be clear, transparent and easy for consumers to understand. The complete pricing information should be visible at contract formation (in this case, when the user clicks “Start Ride“)
* In the designs shared, the service fee is effectively 'click-wrapped' such that many users would not be aware of this fee at the moment that they enter the contract. This is likely to present a high risk under national consumer law in many EU markets. 
* I suggested three options:
** Add the 0.06 to the “unlock fee“ - it is effectively the same charge and this amount is clearly and transparently communicated to our users.
** Abandon the fee.
** Accept the risk and take steps to mitigate.
* Suggestions to make the fee more defensible included the following:
** Change the “service fee“ to a “Short-Ride Fee“;
** Change the fee from applying to all rides, to instead being a conditional charge, similar to those found in the extended card (e.g. reservation fee, pause fee etc). For example, if a ride is shorter than 3-8 minutes, it is considered a “short-ride“ and the fee applies. 
** Change the “i“ symbol on the scooter card to a more clear call to action for users to become aware of the additional fees that apply to the service aside from the base minute rate. Examples would be clickable text “show fees“ or “more fee info“ or “view full fees and charges“
** Change the extended scooter card to better disclose additional conditional charges (for example, the “Parking Enforcement Fee“ or the “Restricted Parking Area Fee“)
